scientific_question: For every one of the 256 already executed R preprocessing seeds, distinguish source-confirmed positive evidence that survived the resample from positive evidence lost by the processing channel, and certify the direction of finite-world compatibility under positive-only evidence.

source.original_study: Mizsei and Wenner (2025), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15044115; CC BY 4.0

fixed_grain.q1: 27 original analysis sites; 144 native-positive species×site pairs
fixed_grain.q2: 13 intervention sites; 77 native-positive species×site pairs, nested in Q1
fixed_grain.observation_key: site, species; source-positive if any original native survey count >0
fixed_grain.processing: R 4.4.3; upstream pinned survreps; 20 pseudo-row site normalization; original 256 seeds 1..256

outcomes: source-positive pair count and source-anchored coverage on each seed
256-seed intersection (retained in all 256), variable (lost in at least one but retained in at least one), and never-retained (lost in all 256)
per-species descriptive retained/loss frequencies with source positive denominators
exact for each seed S subset O and recovered=S union (O minus S) equals O
if pseudo-zero falsely interpreted as biological absence, exactly |O minus S| contradictions with source-confirmed positives; not actual ecological world exclusion
generic finite-world positive-only monotonicity W(O) subset W(S), demonstrated in unit tests and in explanation, without inventing ecological world counts
stops: No real EOG movement/viability/biotic world set is estimated from these processing records.
Never interpret absent-from-pseudo observation as biological absence.
These 256 seeds are a retrospective processing sensitivity, not independent ecological replicates or new EOG-WF endpoint.
Never infer true ecological world counts from unconstrained binary masks or from the seed ensemble.
Maintain the Draft review boundary and do not merge.
